name: SuperDoc
kind: Document engine for DOCX, built directly on OOXML
leads: Use SuperDoc to edit a Word file and get it back intact
detail: Use SuperDoc when a document must come back from the browser unchanged: it saved the trial's test file with nothing lost, and Word draws the result exactly like the original. It is AGPL-3.0, and it kept five of ten hostile test files, so screen what you open.
renderSection: 2.1 SuperDoc — the closest thing to a Word clone

name: Folio
kind: Browser editor and framework-neutral OOXML engine
leads: Use Folio for redline review, but check Word opens it
detail: Use Folio for redline review in the browser: it shows every change with author and date, and it returned 34 of the test file's 35 parts untouched. Word refused the file it saved from the trial's test document, because of how it writes a tracked move, so try your own files in Word first.

name: GenOffice
kind: Open-source AI Office suite: Docs, Sheets, Slides and PDF
leads: Use GenOffice for a whole office suite that stays quick
detail: Use GenOffice if you want Docs, Sheets and Slides in one open-source desktop suite: it kept every part of the test file and opened 500,000 words in about 3 seconds. It lost the text of two merged table cells and kept seven of ten hostile test files, so keep untrusted documents away from it.
renderSection: 2.3 GenOffice — the only editor that draws the SmartArt's node texts

name: eigenpal
license: Apache-2.0 (Pro packages under the EigenPal Pro License)
kind: Document engine with React and Vue adapters and an Office.js-style Editor API
leads: Use eigenpal for a quick editor that saves clean Word files
detail: Use eigenpal (docx-editor.dev) when speed matters: it stayed quick from 500 to 500,000 words, and it saved the test file with nothing lost, pixel for pixel in Word. Showing deleted words in a redline needs its paid Pro package, and so does the server-side Editor API.

name: office-open
kind: Typed generator and parser for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument
leads: Use office-open to generate Word files, not to edit them
detail: Use office-open to build or parse Office documents in code: it is a library with no editing screen, and it kept every word of the test file. Do not pass existing files through it and back: Word refused its saved output, and it could not read that output in again.
renderSection: 2.6 Office-Open — a library, not an editor

name: Docen
kind: Editor on TipTap, ProseMirror and LeaferJS that paginates by Word's stacking rules
leads: Use Docen for short documents and experiments only
detail: Use Docen to try a canvas editor that pages like Word on short files: it kept nearly all the text and matched Word's 6 pages. Its own README says it is not ready for production, Word refused the file it saved, and the 500-page sample opens but leaves the tab unresponsive for minutes.
renderSection: 2.5 Docen — right page count, wrong chart

name: WordCraft
kind: Native word processor in Rust, with its own layout engine
leads: Use WordCraft for speed and charts, not yet for redlines
detail: Use WordCraft when raw speed matters: it opened and saved 250,000 words in about a quarter of a second, and Word opens what it saves. It lost part of the tracked-change history and some text of the test file, so it is not for review work yet.
renderSection: 2.7 WordCraft — its own renderer, and it is very good

name: Fidus Writer
kind: Academic writing tool; the measured tree is its schema, importer and exporter
leads: Use Fidus Writer for academic publishing, not Word files
detail: Use Fidus Writer to write papers and export them to JATS, LaTeX or EPUB; it also handled the hostile test files best in the trial. It is not a tool for existing Word files: its import drops every table, and Word refused the file it saved.
renderSection: 2.11 Fidus Writer — the text renders, the table does not exist

name: Plate.js
kind: Plugin framework for rich-text editors, with a headless DOCX import and export
leads: Use Plate to build your own editor; it says what it drops
detail: Use Plate.js to build a web editor of your own: it is the only tool in the trial that lists what it could not keep, and by default it refuses a file instead of damaging it. It is not for passing Word files through: headers, footnotes, comments, pictures and tracked changes are lost.

name: docs.plus
kind: Real-time collaborative editor with a chatroom on every heading
leads: Use docs.plus to write together, not to keep Word files
detail: Use docs.plus for live group writing, with a chat on every heading; Word opens the files it exports. Do not send it a document under review: importing destroys tracked changes without warning, and most of a Word file's structure is gone after saving.
renderSection: 2.10 docs.plus — the corpus arrives as HTML

name: canvas-editor
kind: Canvas and SVG editor that owns its whole rendering pipeline
leads: Use canvas-editor for short new documents, not Word files
detail: Use canvas-editor for documents written from scratch: short files open in under half a second and scrolling stays smooth. It is not for existing Word files: it crashed on the trial's test table, it has no tracked changes, and long documents overwhelm it.
renderSection: 2.8 Canvas-Editor — the body does not render

name: Docxodus
kind: Structure-aware OOXML engine for .NET, WebAssembly, npm and Python
leads: Use Docxodus for exact Word rendering and solid redlines
detail: Use Docxodus if the page must match Word: it saved the test file with nothing changed, Word draws its output pixel for pixel, and it shows tracked changes and comments in full. Very long documents open slowly in the browser, and it draws a labelled box for equations and SmartArt.
renderSection: 2.13 Docxodus — the engine that draws what it cannot render

name: Apryse WebViewer
kind: Commercial JavaScript document SDK; its DOCX Editor runs Apryse's office engine as WebAssembly
leads: Use Apryse if you can buy a license and want Word's pages
detail: Use Apryse WebViewer if a commercial SDK fits: on screen it drew the test file on Word's 6 pages, and Word draws its saved output almost exactly. Every figure is for a file stamped by the trial license; it dropped 5 of 35 parts and hung on three hostile test files.
renderSection: 2.14 Apryse WebViewer — Word's pages, and a trial stamp on every one

name: react-docx
kind: Paged Word viewer and editor for React, on a Rust parser compiled to WebAssembly
leads: Use react-docx to show and review Word files in React
detail: Use react-docx to put a paged Word viewer and editor in a React app: it showed the 500-page sample on 500 pages in under 9 seconds, with review cards for changes and comments. The trial has not yet measured what it keeps when it saves, so try a round trip before relying on it.

name: Univer
kind: Office SDK with a canvas document editor; its .docx import and export are in a separate Server SDK
leads: Use Univer for documents born in it; it cannot open .docx
detail: Use Univer if you are building an office app and the documents start inside it. Its open-source packages cannot read or write Word files, which takes its separately licensed Server SDK, and tracked changes are not shown.

name: OpenDoc
kind: Rust engine in WebAssembly that reads, lays out, paints and saves DOCX, with its own editor; pre-release
leads: Watch OpenDoc: quick on long files, still pre-release
detail: Use OpenDoc to evaluate a Rust engine that loaded the 500-page sample in about 3.5 seconds, shows each change with accept and reject, and can draw pages on a server. It is a pre-release that is hard to embed today, and the trial has not yet measured what it keeps when it saves.

name: BetterOffice
kind: Rust OOXML engines in WebAssembly, run in a background worker, with a React editor
leads: Use BetterOffice for a responsive editor on long files
detail: Use BetterOffice if the page must stay responsive: its engine runs in a background worker, showed the 500-page sample on 500 pages in about 8 seconds, and can also draw pages on a server. The trial has not yet measured what it keeps when it saves, so try a round trip first.

name: OnlyOffice (CryptPad build)
maker: Ascensio System (ONLYOFFICE); this build by CryptPad (XWiki)
kind: OnlyOffice's document editor and its converter, built to run wholly in the browser with no document server
leads: Use OnlyOffice for a full Word-like editor, if AGPL fits
detail: Use this build for a complete, familiar editor that runs wholly in the browser and shows redlines in each author's colour. It is AGPL-3.0 and heavy, about 3 seconds and an 18 MB download for a 3-page file, and the trial has not yet measured what it keeps when it saves.

name: Nutrient Web SDK
kind: Commercial SDK that converts a Word file to PDF in the browser and displays it; view-only
leads: Use Nutrient to show Word files as PDF, not to edit them
detail: Use Nutrient Web SDK if you only need to display a Word file: it converts the file to PDF inside the browser. It cannot edit or show tracked changes, it substitutes fonts, and it loads about 105 MB before the first page.

name: LibreOffice
kind: The baseline: a full office suite, converted headlessly
leads: Use LibreOffice as the yardstick, and to convert in bulk
detail: Use LibreOffice for conversion on a server or desktop: it reproduced Word's 6 pages and kept every word of the test file. It rewrites the file as its own, dropping 10 of 35 parts, and it is the trial's baseline, not a browser editor.
